title: The Escarpment of the Sepik Basin
premise: Ines Halloran, a disgraced railroad engineer hiding from a debt and a scandal in Port Moresby, is hired to run the radio schedule for a survey expedition charting closed rail lines through the Sepik Basin. When the expedition goes silent upriver, Ines must follow their route alone, guided by an inherited compass that belonged to the father who abandoned him. He finds the survivors guarding evidence that the concession's backers engineered the disaster to bury proof of falsified permits, and he must choose between exposing them and protecting the men who trusted him. The novel ends with Ines delivering the expedition home and surrendering the evidence to a journalist on the day the permits expire, choosing justice over his own anonymity.
about_author: Petra Kavanagh is the pen name of a former field engineer who spent six years on infrastructure projects across Papua New Guinea before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose professional competence is the only thing standing between them and ruin.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Ines Halloran, POV. Ines takes a low-visibility job scheduling radios for a survey expedition, hoping his debts and disgrace stay buried. Studying the expedition's maps of decommissioned rail lines, he recognizes his father's handwriting in the margin annotations. Emotional beat: wary detachment cracking into unease as the past surfaces.

chapters.title: Compass Bearing
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Packing the expedition's spare kit, Ines finds a brass compass engraved with his surname, shipped to him by a lawyer after his father's death. He tests it against the old rail alignments and it points consistently off true north, toward something unmarked. Emotional beat: resentment braided with reluctant curiosity about the father he despises.

chapters.title: Last Scheduled Transmission
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. The expedition's daily check-in from a camp above the Karawari tributary cuts off mid-sentence. Company protocol says wait forty-eight hours; Ines's reading of the terrain says something is wrong now. His supervisor orders silence. Emotional beat: the first real decision, duty versus instinct.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Ines spends two days listening to static, cross-referencing weather reports and river gauges, and concludes the camp site was mischarted by at least ten kilometers. He quietly copies the concession files before resigning. Emotional beat: cold resolve; he stops being an employee and becomes an investigator.

chapters.title: The Wewak Ferry
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Traveling north under a false work order, Ines falls in with Marta Ondoua, a geologist who was meant to join the expedition but was bumped at the last minute by the company's financier. She suspects she was excluded deliberately. Emotional beat: cautious alliance between two people who don't trust institutions.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Hiring a boatman named Tobias, Ines follows the expedition's logged route past villages where the surveyors were seen arguing with men flying the concession company's colors. The compass pulls him toward an unmapped spur line. Emotional beat: mounting dread as the wilderness confirms the map's lies.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta reconstructs the financier's paper trail: the concession permits expire in nineteen days, and the company has been logging ore reserves along land it never legally held. She realizes the 'survey' was cover for a land grab. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Spur Line
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Ines finds the ghost railway his father helped build and abandon, its culverts dynamited from behind, and understands someone wanted this route erased from memory. Fresh boot prints and a burned supply cache say the expedition passed here recently. Emotional beat: eerie recognition; he is walking his father's failure in reverse.

chapters.title: Signals in the Static
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. At night Ines catches a fragmentary transmission: three survivors using the expedition's emergency code, moving toward the spur line. They are being followed. He answers against every rule of tradecraft, revealing his position to save theirs. Emotional beat: commitment; there is no invisible way out now.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: Rhys Calloway, the concession's security chief. Calloway reports to the financier that the survivors have the original permit surveys proving falsification, and that a rogue engineer is loose on the spur line. He requests permission to make the problem permanent. Emotional beat: chilling bureaucratic calm over casual violence.

chapters.title: Reunion at the Culvert
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Ines reaches the survivors: expedition leader Dr. Amara Sesay, injured; two guides; and a box of documents they nearly died carrying. Sesay doesn't trust him until he recites her own check-in codes back to her. Emotional beat: fragile trust forged under threat.

chapters.title: The Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Among the documents is a ledger in his father's hand, recording bribes he took to falsify the original alignments decades ago, and a confession he never sent. Ines must reconcile the man who ruined him with the man who tried, too late, to make it right. Emotional beat: grief and fury colliding into something like forgiveness.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta meets the group at a mission station and lays out the arithmetic: if the permits lapse without the fraud being documented publicly, the company refiles clean and wins forever. They need eleven days of travel and one journalist who will print it. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: Calloway, POV. Calloway's trackers pick up the group's trail. He burns the mission station's boat to strand them, forcing the party into the swamps. Emotional beat: predator patience; the antagonist plays the long game because the law is on his side.

chapters.title: Through the Sago Swamps
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. A grueling crossing: leeches, fever, Sesay worsening. Ines uses his engineering knowledge to rig crossings and read the water, earning the guides' respect. The compass, checked nightly, keeps pointing to a junction ahead. Emotional beat: leadership earned through competence and care.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Junction
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. At the old rail junction the compass was pointing to, Ines finds his father's hidden cache: duplicate originals of every falsified document, plus correspondence implicating the financier directly. Calloway's men ambush them; a guide is killed covering the escape. Emotional beat: triumph poisoned by loss.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Calloway, POV. Calloway corners the weakened party and offers Ines a deal: the documents for the debt wiped clean and his name restored. Ines asks for one night to decide. Emotional beat: temptation rendered honestly; the offer would genuinely save him.

chapters.title: What Ines Halloran Carries
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Ines weighs the bargain against the dead guide, his father's ledger, and Sesay's quiet statement that some debts aren't paid in money. He declines at dawn and the party scatters Calloway's boats with a sabotaged fuel cache. Emotional beat: identity chosen at last; he knows who he is when it costs him.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. A desperate downriver run with Calloway pursuing, Tobias piloting, and Sesay fading. Marta radios the journalist from a ridge with a partial transmission, gambling that fragments will force a story before the company can suppress it. Emotional beat: white-knuckle momentum toward the deadline.

chapters.title: Permits Expiring
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. They reach the coast on the final day. Calloway makes one last attempt to seize the documents at the wharf; Tobias and the guides hold him off while Ines delivers everything to the journalist as the permits legally lapse. Emotional beat: climax resolved not by violence but by timing, testimony, and nerve.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Weeks later: the financier is indicted, the concession voided, the survivors testifying. Marta reflects on how close justice came to failing and on the ordinary courage that tipped it. Emotional beat: exhausted, unsentimental satisfaction.

chapters.title: True North
chapters.summary: Ines, POV. Ines buries his father's compass at the repaired spur-line culvert, keeping only the ledger to give Sesay's family closure. Taking honest work rebuilding the line, he stops running. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; inheritance reclaimed as responsibility rather than shame.
